2. Short facts of the case are as follows : The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit being Title Suite No. 15 of 2002 in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Chandpur Sadar, Chandpur impleading the opposite parties as defendants therein for declaration that the so-called order dated 21-11-2004 passed by the opposite parties compulsorily retiring the plaintiff-petitioner from service is illegal, and not binding upon the petitioner, stating, in short, that the petitioner passed the Matriculation examination in the year, 1961 from Shahatoli High School and after getting the Matriculation Certificate he observed that in the Matriculation certificate his date of birth has wrongly been written and being conversant of the aforesaid wrong entry of his date of birth in the Matriculation certificate, the father of the petitioner being dead, his elder brother Abdul Mannan Tafader appearing before the Magistrate, 1st Class Chandpur had sworn an affidavit on 3-7-1963 correcting his date of birth as 3-1-1945; that thereafter when he applied for the past of B Com teacher, in his application he recorded his date of birth as 3-1-1945 and on the basis of interview, he was appointed as BCom teacher on 5-8-1966 and joined the duty on 8-8-1966. That the plaintiff while serving in that school as B.com teacher, in course of time, he became senior teacher and he was included in the Government M PO Register on 1-1-1981 and his index No. is 110555 and his Institutional Code No. is 07011101205, that accordingly, in all registers his date of birth was recorded as 3-1-1945 and that in the office of the Deputy Director General of the Department of Education, and Assistant Director, Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board, attested his date of birth to be 3-1-1945 and that, the petitioner was elected in the School Managing Committee as teacher representative for certain terms, where it was shown that the plaintiff should be able to serve up to 18-1-2005 as, according to existing Rule a teacher can serve upto the age of 60 years; that the petitioner was elected in the Managing Committee for a few terms and while represented in that capacity, there cropped up certain difference of opinion with some members of the School Managing Committee and following which as a measure of victimization, the petitioner was served with notice that he should retire on 18-1-2001 and in reply of which he clarified his position that being his dare of birth 3-1-1945 he is competent to serve up to 18-1-2005, but without paying any attention to the said reply of petitioner, he was retired vide order dated 22-1-2001 and hence the suit. 

 3. The opposite parties as defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 4-9 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the date of birth of the plaintiff was 19-1-1941 according to his Matriculation certificate which was corrected through an affidavit and he filed an application for the post of teacher in 1966 and in his application he wrote date of birth as on 3-1-1945 and he also enclosed the said affidavit dated 3-7-1963; but the plaintiff did not file any petition to the concerned Education Board for correction of his date of birth as was in the Matriculation certificate; that on 17-11-2001; there was an audit enquiry in the school and it was found that the plaintiffs date of birth according to Matriculation Certificate is 19-1-1941, but the plaintiff did not show any corrected legal documents and in that audit report the date of birth was written as 19-1-1941 in the list of teacher and other staffs working bio-data and the plaintiff agreed and signed there; that in that capacity the plaintiff attained the age of 60 years on 18-1-2001, but he served there, by. managing the authority of the school, that on 22-11-2001 by taking a decision in a Managing Committee meeting, the plaintiff was directed to show the legal documents about his date of birth, but the plaintiff was unable to do the same, thus a direction was given to the plaintiff-petitioner for retirement from the service as a teacher and the petitioner signed and agreed and, as such, the notice of retirement was served upon him; thus the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The learned trial Court on consideration of the evidence and materials on record decreed the suit. As against that the defendant preferred Title Appeal No.3 of 2004 in the court of the learned District Judge, Chandpur and the learned District Judge, by his judgment and decree dated 25-4-2004 allowed the appeal and thereby set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid appellate judgment and decree, the plaintiff-petitioner obtained the present Rule. Mr. Md Abul Kalam Patwary the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner placed the revisional application, the impugned judgment and decree, the deposition of the PWs and DWs and submitted that the learned trial Court having considered the deposition of the PWs and DWs and the materials on record decreed the suit but the learned appellate Court without considering the deposition of the PWs and DWs allowed the appeal. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submitted that the plaintiff joined the defendant School on 8-8-1966 and in his application he stated his date of birth was 3-1-1945 as supported by an affidavit dated 3-7-1963 and that he served the school for 36 years with full satisfaction of the authority and the defendants having accepted his date of birth as 3-1-1945 paid him salary for such a long period on the basis of the monthly payment order (MPO), the defendants cannot be allowed to say now the date of retirement of the plaintiff will be calculated from 19-1-1941 as shown in his Matriculation Certificate of the year 1961, and the learned trial Court having considered all these papers and documents having decreed the suit, the learned appellate Court committed an error in law in allowing the appeal without considering at all this aspect of the case. 

 6. On perusal of the judgment passed by the learned trial Court, it appears, the learned trial Court, on consideration of the evidence and the materials on record, held that the defendants appointed the plaintiff as teacher in the said School on scrutiny/consideration of his Matriculation certificate along with the affidavit dated 3-7-1963; that the affidavit was sworn on 3-7-1963 much before joining the service on 8-8-1966; that since the plaintiff did not inform the relevant Education Board for correction of his age as per affidavit dated 3-7-1963 showing his date of birth on 3-1-1945, it cannot be said that the affidavit is liable to be cancelled, inasmuch as at that time there was no Rules or provisions for amendment of the age by the concerned Education Board; that since the defendants appointed the plaintiff knowing fully about his amended age and he served the defendant School for 36 years and there is no objection by anybody else so long, now it cannot be said by the defendants that he should get retirement from service on the basis of his age as per Matriculation certificate showing his date of birth as 19-1-1941; and that the plaintiff having been present in the meeting wherein decision was taken by the Managing Committee of the school as to the discrepancy of his age as per Matriculation certificate of the plaintiff, and he was present in the said meeting by putting his signature it cannot be said that now the suit by the plaintiff is not maintainable. On these findings the learned trial Court decreed the suit. 

 8. Admittedly as per Matriculation certificate of the plaintiff his date of birth is 19-1-1941, admittedly the plaintiffs brother had sworn an affidavit on 3-7-1963 stating that his date of birth was wrongly recorded in his Matriculation certificate as 19-1-1941 that the actual date of birth of the plaintiff is 3-1-1945, admittedly the plaintiff joined as a teacher of the defendant school on 8-8-1966 and admittedly the monthly pay order (MPO) of the plaintiff started with effect from 1-1-1981 and admittedly, he served the school for more than 36 years and he got his salary from the government through MPO for more than 20 years and admittedly, during this long period of time none raised any objection about his date of birth as shown on 3-1-1945 vide affidavit on 3-7-1963. After these 36 years it is said that as per audit report an objection has been raised as to his age of his retirement and that his date of retirement according to the defendants will be 18-1-2001 on the basis of his age as recorded in his Matriculation certificate as 19-1-1941 and not as recorded vide the affidavit on 3-1-1945. 

 10. The learned appellate Court it appears, on the other hand, did not consider the deposition of the PWs and DWs on record and also did not consider that the plaintiff got his service on the basis of the affidavit dated 3-7-1963 showing his date of birth as 3-1-1945 and that he got his salary through MPO for each month prepared by the defendants for such a long time. It may be noted that though the defendants stated that there was an objection by the audit authority but it appears, for the last 20 years there was such audit report but no such objection was ever raised. Further, it shows that in the audit report for the relevant period of 1999-2002 Exhibit Kha series, in fact, no objection was raised as to the age of the plaintiff 

 11. It appears, the learned appellate Court mainly considered the fact that the plaintiff as per his affidavit (Exhibit 2) did not get corrected his age in the Matriculation certificate (Exhibit 1) from the concerned Education Board and held that in the absence of such correction his age recorded in the Matriculation certificate will be the basis for calculation of his retiring age. It is true that the plaintiff did not get corrected his age in the Matriculation certificate issued by the concerned Education Board. According to the plaintiff, there was no such mandatory provision for correction 'of age at the relevant time by the Education Board. The Regulation/Rule for such correction in the Matriculation certificate was promulgated by the Board subsequently. However, the fact is that, the Matriculation Certificate of the plaintiff was not corrected but there was an affidavit to the effect that the date of his birth is 3-1-1945 and this affidavit was accepted by the defendants and the defendants allowed him to join the service and allowed him to get salary for 36 years, and gave his salary by MPO issued by the defendants for the last 20 years without any objection from anybody and it was within the full knowledge of the defendants. So, now, the defendants cannot be allowed to say that his date of birth wil1 be calculated on the basis of the Matriculation Certificate and not from date shown in his affidavit (Exhibit 3). 

 12. The facts, the evidence and materials on record show that the defendants having full knowledge of the correction of the age of the plaintiff by the Affidavit (Exhibit 3) the defendants allowed him to serve for the last 36 years and allowed him to get his salary by MPO for 20 years and, as such, in my opinion, the defendants are estopped as per provision of section 115 of the Evidence Act to say the contrary Reference may be given to the cases reported in 42 DLR 533. 46 DLR 268 and 1 BLC 375 wherein it has been held that when one person/persons (here the defendants) by their act allowed the other person/persons (here the plaintiff) to do something and on good faith the other person (here the plaintiff) has served or acted as per assurance of that person (here the defendants) that person (here the defendants) cannot be allowed to deny their (defendants) declaration or act. In the present case, the defendants having allowed the plaintiff to serve the school for 36 years on the basis of his age as per affidavit (Exhibit 3), they now cannot be a\1owed to say that his retiring age should be calculated from his age as given in Matriculation Certificate (Exhibit 1) and not from the affidavit (Exhibit 3). 

 15. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. Send down the lower court records at once.
